fixes.explanation: Read it again, friend, because this one is true. Jacob says of Simeon and Levi, “May I never enter their council; may I never join their assembly.” (Genesis 49:6). He gives his reason right there: “For they kill men in their anger…” I think this is one of the hard moments in the whole blessing.

Think of a bow, friend. Jacob says Joseph “steadied his bow,” and his strong arms “…were tempered by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob…” (Genesis 49:24). That's God's own hands on Joseph's strength. Then Jacob piles on more names: “…the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel…” I'd say Joseph didn't hold steady on his own power. The Mighty One was holding him.

An eagle, friend? That's a good-looking bird, but Jacob never says it. He says “Benjamin is a ravenous wolf…” (Genesis 49:27). Eagles fly in, grab something and glide off. The wolf eats the prey in the morning and divides the plunder in the evening. I think I'd take the wolf over my own mustache when it's near my cookie box. WOLF, baker.

Egypt makes sense, friend. Jacob has been living there, and that's where his son Joseph is. But he points somewhere else. The cave is “…in the land of Canaan.” (Genesis 49:30). It's the field Abraham bought, with Abraham, Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah already buried there (Genesis 49:31). I think Jacob is asking to be laid to rest with his family, and that's a tender thing to ask.
